newsitem.title: UK: Commonwealth group to meet on rights, democracy.
newsitem.headline: Commonwealth group to meet on rights, democracy.

text.p: The Commonwealth said on Friday it would hold a ministerial meeting in London next week that would discuss human rights in Nigeria, suspended from the grouping after the execution of nine government critics.
It said the foreign ministers would also consider the state of democracy in Gambia and Sierra Leone and prepare for a Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting, to be held in Edinburgh in October.
The so-called Commonwealth Ministerial Action Group on the Harare Declaration, comprising ministers from eight member nations, will hold talks on Monday and Tuesday.
Nigeria was suspended from Commonwealth membership in late 1995 after it executed writer Ken Saro Wiwa and eight other activists. Nigerian authorities accused him of murder.
The ministers will assess a visit by the group to Lagos last November.
The group will review the final phase of Gambia's transition to civilian rule and Sierra Leone's approach to the Commonwealth to provide monitors to oversee its peace process.
